title: Lab 06 — Virtual Grid: Testing 10,000 Rows That Mostly Don't Exist

variants.hint: On the first screen every row's position looks right. Does it still, 5,000 rows down?
variants.debrief: aria-rowindex counted from the top of the rendered window, not the data -- so a screen reader said 'row 4 of 10,000' at row 5,000. It only shows once you leave the first screen.

variants.hint: Go all the way to the bottom. Is the last citation actually there?
variants.debrief: An off-by-one in the virtualiser's range (end index trimmed by 1) meant the last row was never rendered: the scrollbar reached the bottom and showed a blank gap. Boundary rows are where virtualisers break.

variants.hint: The first screen is correct. Check a row the back office told you about -- it's a long way down.
variants.debrief: Past row 5,000 the details were joined off by one: CIT-07342 showed CIT-07343's status and amount. Every row looked plausible; only checking a KNOWN row deep in the data could tell.

variants.hint: How many disputed citations are there, according to someone other than the page?
variants.debrief: The filter only searched the chunks the page had already downloaded (62 matches out of 1,250) -- and its count label agreed with it. The page can't be its own oracle: the API summary is.
